_extraction_metadata.source_publication: Virklund, A.; Nielsen, A. T.; Woodley, J. M. "Biocatalysis with In-Situ Product Removal Improves p-Coumaric Acid Production" ChemBioChem 2024, 25, e202400178.
_extraction_metadata.extraction_method: Manual structured extraction against the STRENDA-Biocatalysis data model. The MCP server's automated 'Extract_Strenda_Biocatalysis' tool could not be used for this run because its input schema was rejected by the API (server-side bug: 'biocatalyst/identity/molecular_weight/minimum must be number'). The full data model was instead retrieved via the compliance/data-model tool and populated by hand from the PDF text.
_extraction_metadata.null_convention: null = not reported anywhere in the main text or figures/tables of the publication (Supporting Information was not available for review). No values were invented.
_extraction_metadata.schema_adaptation: The publication reports FOUR distinct biocatalytic runs (2 biological replicates x with/without ATPS-ISPR) sharing one biocatalyst and largely overlapping methods. Rather than force this into a single StrendaBiocatalysis object, shared elements (biocatalyst, reaction_components, vessel) are given once and the four runs are listed under 'experiments', each populating operation_mode / reaction_conditions / results / sampling for that run.

name: Biocatalysis with In-Situ Product Removal Improves p-Coumaric Acid Production
description: Aqueous two-phase system (ATPS) in-situ product removal (ISPR) coupled to an immobilized whole-cell tyrosine ammonia lyase (FjTAL) biocatalyst to relieve product inhibition and improve p-coumaric acid (pCA) titer from tyrosine, as part of a two-stage bioprocess (fed-batch tyrosine fermentation followed by batch pCA biocatalysis).

identity.name: Tyrosine ammonia lyase from Flavobacterium johnsoniae (FjTAL)
identity.catalyzed_reaction: Tyrosine -> p-coumaric acid + NH3 (ammonia-lyase elimination reaction)

sequences.notes: Referenced only as 'Supporting Information 6' (plasmid sequence), not included in main text.

self_produced_details.plasmid_specifications: E. coli cells cloned to express FjTAL from a plasmid under an arabinose-inducible promoter (full construct details in Supporting Information 6, not in main text).
self_produced_details.purification_method: Purified as described previously in ref. [6] (Virklund et al., Biotechnol. J. 2023, 18, 2300111); method not repeated in this paper's main text.

application.notes: Two distinct application contexts reported: (1) whole-cell immobilized biocatalyst used for preparative pCA biocatalysis in the rotating bed reactor (RBR); (2) purified free enzyme used only for the small-scale specific-activity assay (Figure 2). See 'experiments' and 'characterization_data.activity_vs_salt' below.

concentration.determination_method: Cell loading reported as wet cell mass (see immobilization.loading), not as a molar/mass enzyme concentration.

activity.determination_method: Specific activity of purified FjTAL in standard 50 mM CAPS buffer pH 10, 30°C, 2 mM tyrosine, UV-vis (325 nm); see characterization_data.activity_vs_salt for the full salt-dependence dataset (Figure 2).

workflow_details.cell_disruption_process: None for the RBR biocatalyst (permeabilized, intact whole cells per abstract); cells were disrupted/purified only for the enzyme used in the activity assay (method not detailed in main text, see ref. [6]).
workflow_details.harvesting_method: Fed-batch fermentation of a tyrosine-overproducing/FjTAL-expressing E. coli strain, harvested as described in Supporting Information 7 (not detailed in main text).

immobilization.biocatalyst_state: Whole E. coli cells overexpressing FjTAL (permeabilized)
immobilization.immobilisation_chemistry: Physical entrapment in a polysaccharide hydrogel, ionically cross-linked with potassium ions
immobilization.carrier_material: kappa-carrageenan : locust bean gum (LBG) hydrogel, 2:1 ratio, 1.33% w/v kappa-carrageenan + 0.66% w/v LBG + 0.9% NaCl
immobilization.linkers: Potassium ions (K+, from KCl bath) cross-link the kappa-carrageenan/LBG network
immobilization.immobilisation_method: Wet cells (~14 g in Experiment 1; ~17 g in Experiment 2, from different fermentation batches) thawed and resuspended in 20 mL saline, then mixed with 80 mL of a ~50°C solution of 1.33% w/v kappa-carrageenan, 0.66% w/v locust bean gum, 0.9% NaCl. The mixture was extruded through a 9-needle die (Mesoram, 1 mm inner diameter needles) via peristaltic pump at 33 mL/min, dropped from ~20 cm above a 2% w/v KCl solution warmed to ~37°C and stirred slowly with a magnetic bar. Beads were cross-linked in the KCl bath for 30 minutes without additional heating, then drained and stored overnight at 4°C.
immobilization.purification_method: Drained/washed after cross-linking (no further purification step reported).

loading.unit: g wet cells / 100 mL hydrogel mixture (maximum reported; 14 g used in Experiment 1)
loading.determination_method: Direct wet-mass weighing prior to encapsulation

immobilization.notes: Batch yield ~100 g beads per immobilization batch. Stability: beads reported stable (no visible deterioration/swelling) for 23 h in ~4-6% potassium phosphate solution at 40°C, 200 rpm (main biocatalysis conditions), and separately for 23 h in 25% w/w potassium carbonate at pH 9.9, 40°C, 300 rpm (Supporting Information 4, a harsher stress test). Calcium-alginate beads were tested as a comparator and found unstable in the salt phase (ion-exchange of Ca2+ with K+, forming insoluble calcium phosphate/carbonate; Supporting Information 4). Further cross-linking with glutaraldehyde and poly(ethyleneimine) is suggested as a possible future stability improvement but was NOT performed in this study.

storage.notes: Immobilized bead storage only ('stored overnight at 4°C'); no separate storage protocol given for free enzyme or cell stocks.

amount.unit: g per RBR batch (~980-970 mL total working volume); 2 mM in the activity assay

reaction_components.notes: Described qualitatively as having 'low solubility... even at moderately alkaline pH'; no numeric solubility limit given.

amount.unit: product; spiked at 100 µM, 4%, and 2.5% in various ATPS partition-coefficient screening experiments

reaction_components.notes: Reaction product; the STRENDA role enum has no explicit 'product' value (only substrate/cosubstrate/cofactor/coenzyme/buffer/salt/solvent/ion/other), so 'other' is used here. Charge at pH 10 calculated (Henderson-Hasselbalch) to be 0.47 lower than tyrosine (Supporting Information 1, value not detailed in main text).

amount.unit: 5% w/w in final ATPS ISPR formulation; 10-20% w/w tested for FjTAL activity impact (Figure 2); 30 g K2HPO4 + ~10 g K3PO4 used in the ATPS RBR run; ~10 g K3PO4 used for pH control in the non-ATPS RBR run

reaction_components.notes: Also used as the pH-stat titrant (50% w/V K3PO4 solution) to hold pH at setpoint automatically during the RBR reactions.

amount.unit: 10-20% w/w tested for activity impact; cloud point 5-5.7% w/w (Table 1)

reaction_components.notes: Alternative alkaline salt screened; not used in the final selected ATPS (phosphate system chosen instead).

reactor_specifics.catalyst_localisation: Immobilized whole-cell beads retained within a rotating basket (rotating bed reactor, RBR) so the biocatalyst is physically separated from the bulk liquid/ATPS phases.
reactor_specifics.temperature_control: Reactor contents adjusted/held at 40°C (method not further specified, e.g. jacketed vessel or water bath not stated).

vessel.notes: 1 L rotating bed reactor (RBR), Spinchem, used identically for both the with- and without-ATPS runs in each experiment.

mechanical.stirring_type: Rotating bed (RBR basket rotation, not a conventional impeller)
mechanical.notes: RBR rotated at 200 rpm during the biocatalysis runs. (A separate bead-stability stress test used 300 rpm vortexing per Supporting Information 4, and a 200 rpm stirring stability test is also mentioned in the Discussion.)

feeding.description: Automatic pH-stat addition of 50% w/V K3PO4 solution to hold pH at setpoint; no substrate feeding (single charge of tyrosine at t=0).

monoliquid.solvent_description: Aqueous slurry: 850 mL deionized water + 50 g tyrosine

phases.material_description: Aqueous tyrosine slurry (850 mL DI water, 50 g tyrosine, ~10 g K3PO4)
~100 g immobilized FjTAL whole-cell kappa-carrageenan/LBG beads

samples.notes: Sampled hourly initially, then again at ~21 h; reactor terminated at ~22 h. pCA quantified via absorbance at 385 nm (or 325 nm depending on assay) against a pCA standard curve, samples diluted 20-fold in 50 mM CAPS pH 10, 30°C.

yield_and_conversion.notes: Final pCA titer 11.4 g/L at ~22 h (Table 2/partition-phase breakdown does not apply - single phase).

results.notes: Same batch of immobilized cells as the paired ATPS run below (~14 g wet cells).

phases.material_description: Salt (aqueous) phase: 730 mL DI water + 50 g tyrosine + 30 g K2HPO4 (+ ~10 g K3PO4 for pH)

strategy.notes: Both phases sampled separately after phase separation at reactor termination, in addition to routine dispersion sampling during the run.

samples.notes: Hourly + 21 h sample of the dispersion; at ~22 h reactor stopped, ATPS allowed to settle, salt and polymer phases sampled and their volumes measured separately.

yield_and_conversion.notes: Overall pCA concentration 11.9 g/L; yield 0.238 +/- 0.053 g pCA / g tyrosine (Table 2, Experiment 1).

results.notes: Salt-phase volume 500 mL, concentration 8.2 +/- 1.9 g/L; polymer-phase volume 300 mL, concentration 18.0 +/- 1.9 g/L; partition coefficient (polymer/salt) = 2.19 (Table 2). Initial rate slightly lower than the no-ATPS control but final titer similar - authors note titers were likely too low in this experiment for product inhibition to be significant.

phases.material_description: ~100 g immobilized FjTAL whole-cell beads (higher-activity cell batch, ~17 g wet cells)

yield_and_conversion.notes: Final pCA titer 17.7 g/L at ~23 h.

results.notes: Same batch of immobilized cells (higher activity) as the paired ATPS run below (~17 g wet cells).

feeding.description: Automatic pH-stat addition of 50% w/V K3PO4 solution to hold pH at setpoint.

phases.material_description: Salt (aqueous) phase: 730 mL DI water + 50 g tyrosine + 30 g K2HPO4 (+ ~10 g K3PO4 for pH)

strategy.notes: Final salt/polymer phase separation and separate sampling at reactor termination.

samples.notes: Hourly + 21 h + termination (~22-23 h) sampling; final drained contents settled in a preheated measuring cylinder for phase volume determination.

yield_and_conversion.notes: Overall pCA concentration 33.1 g/L (calculated from phase data, consistent with 33.3 g/L direct dispersion sampling and the abstract's headline '33 g/L within 24 hours'); yield 0.724 +/- 0.116 g pCA / g tyrosine (Table 2, Experiment 2). This is the paper's best result: a 1.9-fold titer improvement vs. the no-ATPS control (33.3 vs 17.7 g/L).

results.notes: Salt-phase volume 550 mL, concentration 24.57 g/L (24.6 +/- 1.9 g/L in Table 2); polymer-phase volume 325 mL, concentration 47.58 g/L (47.6 +/- 1.9 g/L); partition coefficient (polymer/salt) = 1.94. Authors note the salt-phase pCA concentration (24.5 g/L) still exceeded the no-ATPS monophase titer (17.7 g/L), suggesting the simple product-inhibition-relief explanation is incomplete; they hypothesize a third partition equilibrium between the hydrogel bead interior and the bulk salt phase (bead pore size may exclude the ~127.5 kDa PEGRPG polymer while still allowing pCA to partition).

kinetics.notes: No Km, kcat, or Ki values are measured/reported in this paper; product inhibition of FjTAL by pCA is discussed qualitatively (competitive, via active-site occupancy, possibly reverse-reaction catalysis) and precise Ki determination is explicitly described as impractical for high-throughput screening (requires many replicates across substrate/product concentrations). Quantitative KM/Ki values for FjTAL are cited as being reported in ref. [6] (a separate publication), not this one.

activity.notes: See characterization_data.activity_vs_salt below for the full Figure 2 dataset (activity vs. salt type/concentration).

yield_and_conversion.notes: See per-experiment results above; best overall yield 0.724 +/- 0.116 g pCA/g tyrosine (Experiment 2, with ATPS).

results.notes: Aggregate/top-level results view; see 'experiments' array for the four individual runs and 'characterization_data' for supporting screening datasets.

activity_vs_salt_Figure2.description: Specific activity of purified FjTAL (µmol pCA min^-1 g^-1 TAL, i.e. U/g) measured in buffer vs. increasing potassium carbonate (CO3) or potassium phosphate (PO4) concentration. Assay: 1 µg purified FjTAL, 2 mM tyrosine, pH 10, 30°C, monitored at 325 nm. Means of duplicates; error bars = 95% CI from pooled SD.
activity_vs_salt_Figure2.note_on_values: Numeric activity values were read approximately from Figure 2 bar chart (paper does not tabulate them); the -19%/-37% figures for phosphate are given exactly in the main text.

initial_screens.system: 15% w/w PEG 8000 : 15% w/w Dextran, 100 µM pCA, room temperature
15% w/w PEG 8000 : 15% w/w K2HPO4, 100 µM pCA, room temperature

cloud_points_Table1.conditions: 40°C, pH 10, starting from 20% polymer / 8% salt / 4% pCA, diluted to cloud point

partition_coefficients_Figure3.conditions: 20% polymer/8% K-phosphate/4% pCA, or diluted to 12.5% polymer/5% K-phosphate/2.5% pCA; single experiment (no replicates)
partition_coefficients_Figure3.note: Values read approximately from Figure 3 bar chart; paper states the final selected 5%/12.5% system's partition coefficient fell further to ~2 once tested in the actual bioreactor (Experiments 1 & 2, Table 2).

process_economics_discussion.conclusion: Polymer cost estimated at ~30% of product value at target titers, indicating polymer recycle is required for economic feasibility. Authors discuss (but did not test) acid crystallization + heating above cloud point, or ultrafiltration, as possible recycle strategies.

not_covered_by_this_paper: Enzyme EC number, molecular weight, and full amino acid/DNA sequence (only referenced via Supporting Information, not present in main text).
Quantitative Km, kcat, kcat/Km, or Ki values for FjTAL (discussed conceptually; values are in a separate prior publication, ref [6]).
Thermodynamic parameters (ΔG, ΔH, ΔS) - not studied.
Selectivity/stereoselectivity parameters - not applicable/reported (TAL forms a single achiral product from tyrosine).
Vessel material, geometry, and closure details for the RBR.
Exact ionic strength values for reaction buffers.
Supplier/purity information for most raw chemicals (tyrosine, phosphate/carbonate salts, NaOH, NaCl) beyond the ATPS polymers and LBG (Sigma-Aldrich).
